chapter: Friends, New York life and recording routine
title: Asked to sing "Jelly Roll Blues" in a Detroit church
summary: A Methodist church on Woodward Avenue asked her to sing "Jelly Roll Blues"; she went through a storm and gave people what they wanted.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: (Inaudible). Now, Jelly Roll -- she sang "Jelly Roll Blues." And I went to a Methodist
Church on Woodward Avenue and they wanted me to sing "Jelly Roll Blues."
In the church. Right there on Woodward Avenue in the 106 -- hundred block.
Well, how do you feel about singing about "Jelly Roll" in church? Would you care?
Well, I didn't want to sing. But they wanted me to sing. (Unintelligible), you know.
They called me. The pastor wasn't there, but if he was, I didn't see him. But all the members was there.
Oh, you went? You did go.
I went. It was storming. It stormed and stormed and I said, "Well, this is a good thing. Can't go." But do you know, that storm left about 9:00 o'clock and they
come and got me? (Laughter.) That's wonderful. I like that.

And they had to wait until I was dressed, because I told them, I say, "Well, I didn't think you all ______." They said, "All the people was there waiting on you, Sip. The people was there waiting on you." So (unintelligible) come in and say, "We heard you was going to be here and we come." And then behind that, they wanted me to sing (unintelligible). So I try to give people what they want.
